title: Error Detection & Spotting the Error
intro: Error detection evaluates a candidate's holistic command over English grammar, syntax, concord, and diction by asking them to locate the incorrect segment in a partitioned sentence (A, B, C, D / No Error). In the WBPSC Clerkship examination, recurring error patterns follow predictable linguistic archetypes that can be swiftly pinpointed through a structured 5-pass scanning methodology.
bengali:
Spotting the Error / Error Detection হলো সরকারি চাকরির ইংরেজি পরীক্ষার সবচেয়ে গুরুত্বপূর্ণ অংশ। এখানে একটি বাক্যকে চার বা পাঁচটি অংশে ভাগ করে দেওয়া হয় (A, B, C, D / No Error) এবং কোন অংশে ভুল আছে তা চিহ্নিত করতে হয়।

WBPSC Clerkship পরীক্ষায় বারবার আসা প্রধান ১০টি ভুলের ধরন:
১. Subject-Verb Agreement-এর ফাঁদ: Subject ও Verb-এর মাঝের Prepositional phrase দেখে বিভ্রান্ত না হয়ে আসল Subject অনুযায়ী Verb বসানো।
২. সময়সূচক শব্দ ও Tense-এর অমিল: বাক্যে 'yesterday', 'ago', 'in 1947' থাকলে Present Perfect (has/have) ব্যবহার করা সম্পূর্ণ ভুল (Simple Past V2 হবে)।
৩. Uncountable Noun-এর সাথে 's' যোগ: Furnitures, informations, sceneries, advices ইত্যাদি লেখা ভুল।
৪. Prepositional Traps: Senior/Junior-এর পরে 'than' লেখা (হবে 'to'); Discuss/Enter/Order-এর পরে অনাবশ্যক Preposition বসানো।
৫. Correlative Conjunction-এর জোড়া ভাঙা: Hardly-র সাথে 'than' লেখা (হবে 'when'); No sooner-এর সাথে 'when' লেখা (হবে 'than')।
৬. Redundant Words (অতিরিক্ত অনাবশ্যক শব্দ): 'Return back' (হবে শুধু 'return'); 'Revert back' (হবে 'revert'); 'Cousin brother/sister' (হবে শুধু 'cousin')।
৭. Conditional Clauses-এ 'Will/Would': If-ক্লজে কখনো 'will' বা 'would have' বসবে না।

rules.rule: THE 5-PASS SCANNING METHODOLOGY for WBPSC Error Detection:
examples: Pass 1 - Subject-Verb Concord: Check every finite verb against its genuine grammatical subject.
Pass 2 - Tense & Timeline: Check if past time adverbs (yesterday, ago) match V2, and verify conditional sequences.
Pass 3 - Pronoun Cases & Agreement: Check nominative vs objective cases after prepositions/than, and pronoun antecedents.
Pass 4 - Prepositions & Conjunctions: Check fixed prepositions (senior to, prevent from) and correlative pairs (hardly... when).
Pass 5 - Nouns & Modifiers: Check uncountable nouns (furniture, advice), misplaced modifiers, and dangling participles.
exceptions: If all 5 passes verify as grammatically sound and idiomatic, choose option 'No Error'.

rules.rule: SUPERFLUOUS / REDUNDANT EXPRESSIONS (Tautology): Words that duplicate meaning must be omitted.
examples: Incorrect: Return back -> Correct: Return (return already means come back).
Incorrect: Revert back -> Correct: Revert.
Incorrect: Cousin brother / Cousin sister -> Correct: Cousin.
Incorrect: Enter into the room -> Correct: Enter the room.
Incorrect: Sufficient enough -> Correct: Sufficient / Enough.
Incorrect: Supposing if you fail -> Correct: Supposing you fail / If you fail.
exceptions: 'Enter into' is correct for figurative agreements or treaties.

rules.rule: MISPLACED MODIFIER ERRORS: An adverb or limiting modifier must be situated immediately adjacent to the word it qualifies.
examples: Incorrect: He only died yesterday (Implies he did nothing else yesterday except die).
Correct: He died only yesterday (Qualifies 'yesterday').
Incorrect: She almost washed all the clothes.
Correct: She washed almost all the clothes.
exceptions: Position of 'ONLY' changes the sentence meaning drastically—verify which constituent it is intended to modify.

rules.rule: DOUBLE COMPARATIVES AND DOUBLE SUPERLATIVES are grammatically incorrect in standard examination English.
examples: Incorrect: He is more taller than his brother. -> Correct: He is taller than his brother.
Incorrect: This is the most best solution. -> Correct: This is the best solution.
Incorrect: She is more wiser than her sister. -> Correct: She is wiser than her sister.

rules.rule: ONE OF THE + PLURAL NOUN + SINGULAR VERB (unless preceded by a relative pronoun):
examples: Standard: 'One of the candidates has cleared the typing test' (Noun is plural 'candidates'; Verb is singular 'has').
With Relative Pronoun: 'He is one of those officers who HAVE performed outstandingly' (Verb agrees with antecedent 'officers', plural).
exceptions: If preceded by 'THE ONLY ONE OF...', the verb reverts to SINGULAR: 'He is the only one of the officers who HAS performed outstandingly'.

commonMistakes: Saying 'She is my cousin sister' instead of 'She is my cousin' (tautology error).
Writing 'Kindly revert back to my email' instead of 'revert to my email' (redundant back).
Writing 'He is more senior than me' instead of 'He is senior to me' (double comparative + wrong preposition).
Writing 'One of my friend is a doctor' instead of 'One of my friends is a doctor' (one of takes plural noun).
Saying 'Supposing if it rains, what will we do?' instead of 'Supposing it rains' (supposing and if cannot coexist).
examTricks: The Redundancy Blacklist: Return back, Revert back, Cousin sister/brother, Repeat again, Supposing if -> INSTANT ERROR.
The 'One of the' Rule: One of the + PLURAL Noun + SINGULAR Verb.
The 'One of those who' Inversion: One of those who + PLURAL Verb; but 'The only one of those who' + SINGULAR Verb.
The 'No Error' Confidence: If passes 1 through 5 check out clean, don't invent errors—select 'No Error'.
memoryTricks: RE- means BACK, so don't write BACK after RE-turn.
revision: Check Subject-Verb agreement first (singular subject = singular verb).
Yesterday, ago -> Simple Past (V2), not has/have.
No redundant words: return back, cousin brother, revert back.
One of the + Plural noun + Singular verb.
No double comparatives: more taller, more better (strictly wrong).
Misplaced 'only': Place 'only' directly before the word it limits.
Senior to, prevent from, agree with/to.
